prompt:
Create a complete Color Picker component system for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, radius, state) - not as separate one-off fields for each variant.

It is a trigger field styled like a text field that shows the currently selected color as a small swatch plus its hex value (e.g. a red square and "#FF031A"). Focusing or clicking the field opens a small palette panel of preset swatch options below it, similar to how Autocomplete and Mention open a floating panel below their field - except this panel is a grid of color swatches instead of a list of text or people rows.

Types (2):
- Outlined: The default color picker style - a bordered box that works well on any background and reads clearly in dense forms.
  Rest: background:#ffffff;border:1.5px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);
  Hover: border-color:#69707D;
  Focus: border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.
- Filled: A softer-emphasis field with a solid background instead of a border, useful when a form sits on a bordered card and an outline would compete visually.
  Rest: background:#f1f1ee;border:1.5px solid transparent;
  Hover: background:#e3e3df;
  Focus: background:#ffffff;border-color:#FF031A;outline:2px solid #ff4253;outline-offset:2px; Never just a color change, so layout never shifts.
  Open: same border/outline treatment as Focus, plus a palette panel of preset color swatches anchored below the field.

States (6, apply to every type): Rest, Hover, Focus, Open, Filled, Disabled.
- Rest/Hover/Focus/Filled: field shows the current color swatch and hex value at all times - there is no empty/placeholder state, a color is always selected.
- Open: the field looks focused and a palette panel is visible directly below it, showing 8 preset color swatches in a grid, with the currently selected swatch visibly marked active via a ring/outline.
- Disabled: 50% opacity, not-allowed cursor, no hover/focus/open feedback.

What size do you want? (24px - XXS / 28px - XS / 32px - S / 36px - SM / 40px - M / 44px - L / 48px - XL / 56px - XXL) Padding and font-size scale proportionally with height.

What corner radius do you want? (0px - Sharp / 4px - Compact / 8px - Balanced / 12px - Soft / Full - Pill) Applies to both Outlined and Filled.

Component properties: Label (editable text above the field), Color value (editable hex text shown next to the swatch, e.g. "#FF031A").

prompt:
Create a complete Notification component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, state) - a corner-anchored card (solid background, border, left accent border, drop shadow, fixed ~260px width) with a semantic icon, a bold title, a longer description line and a close button, used to report a background or async event.

It differs from Toast by carrying more content per instance (icon + title + description + close, and optionally an action) for events the user wasn't necessarily watching for (e.g. "File uploaded successfully", "3 new messages received"), rather than Toast's brief, single-line, self-dismissing confirmation of an action the user just took.

Types (4, drive the left accent border and the icon color - the card itself always stays a solid neutral elevated surface):
- Info: Neutral, informational background event - nothing succeeded or failed, it's just worth surfacing. Accent/icon color: #4f8fe6.
- Success: Confirms a background or async task completed successfully. Accent/icon color: #2fbf6e.
- Warning: Flags something that needs attention but hasn't failed outright. Accent/icon color: #e6a53a.
- Error: Reports that a background or async task failed. Accent/icon color: #ff031a.
Card (same for every type): background:#ffffff;border:1px solid rgba(15,15,10,0.15);border-inline-start:3px solid #4f8fe6;box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.35);

States (3, structural, apply to the whole card):
- Default: icon, title, description and a close (x) button - no action.
- With action: same as Default, plus an inline text-style action button ("Undo") below the description.
- Stacked: shows two of the same notification card layered with a small gap, the second one sitting slightly behind and reduced in opacity, to demonstrate multiple simultaneous notifications.

Component properties: Title (text, default "File uploaded"); Description (text, default "team-report.pdf is ready to share."); Placement (topRight/topLeft/bottomRight/bottomLeft, default topRight - which viewport corner the notification stacks in; multiple notifications in the same placement stack outward from the edge they anchor to).

prompt:
Create a complete Avatar component for the Agentic Design System.

Build it as ONE reusable component controlled by properties (type, size, shape, presence state) - a compact circular (or square) visual identifier for a person, not a one-off image tag.

Content types (3):
- Initials: A colored circle showing the person's 1-2 letter initials - used whenever no photo is available.
- Icon: A colored circle containing a generic person-silhouette icon - a neutral placeholder for an unknown or anonymous person.
- Image: A circle filled with a gradient standing in for an illustrated photo placeholder - real image URLs are never fetched, so this represents where a person's photo would render.

Presence states (4, a small status dot in the bottom-right corner):
- Default: no status dot shown.
- Online: a small green dot.
- Away: a small amber dot.
- Offline: a small gray/dim dot.
These are structural/presentational variants, not interaction states - Avatar itself is not interactive.

Component properties: Size (24px / 32px - default / 40px / 48px, currently 32px - Default - font-size and the status dot scale proportionally with the box size); Shape (Circle / Square, currently Circle); Initials text (Initials type only, currently "JD"). Avatar.Group (a separate composition, not a per-avatar property): a list of Avatars overlapped with negative margin and a border matching the page background, with a Max count past which the final tile becomes a "+N" overflow indicator styled like a real avatar. Show as (Avatars / Names only) - whether the group renders as that overlapping avatar-circle stack, or as a plain vertical list of full names with no avatar graphic at all, for contexts where showing the avatar image isn't worth the space; both modes represent the identical list, including the same "+N" overflow count.
